facts.text: Agent plan writing is the discipline of designing execution plans for AI agent workflows. The harness matters more than the model. Agent completion rates depend more on action-space design, context engineering, and orchestration patterns.
When this skill activates, produce a markdown agent plan containing:
Workflow Overview - what the system does, which orchestration pattern, and why
Agent Roster - each agent's role, model, tools, and context scope
Orchestration Graph - how agents coordinate
Context Budget - token allocation per agent
Safety Constraints - permission boundaries, output validation, human-in-the-loop gates
Evaluation Plan - what to trace, quality metrics
Failure Handling - per-pattern failure modes and recovery strategies
Five patterns dominate production agent systems:
Fan-Out: Parallel execution of independent subtasks. Coordinator dispatches to N agents simultaneously.
Pipeline: Sequential chain where each stage requires the prior stage's output.
Supervisor: A supervisor agent decomposes the task, delegates to specialists, and synthesizes results. The 2026 production default.
Debate: Multiple agents reason independently, then argue toward convergence.
Swarm: Dynamic spawning of agents based on workload.
Agents consume ~7x more tokens than standard chat sessions. Plan token budgets explicitly.
Budget allocation:
System prompt: 500–2,000 tokens. Cached input costs 10–25% of normal.
Tool schemas: Each MCP tool adds 100–500 tokens to context.
Working memory: Reserve 30–50% of context for conversation/reasoning accumulation.
Output headroom: Reserve 15–25% for the agent's response generation.
